glosses.notes: Usually refers to a gold medal won in sports or another competition, and it often stands for the top result after a long period of effort.

examples.sentence: 她把那块金牌放好以后，家里人先没有急着说话，大家更想知道，她在最后那几分钟里到底是怎么坚持过来的。
学校请她回去讲话的时候，她没有一直说金牌有多重要，而是先讲那些最想放弃、却还是得自己站起来的日子。
电视里宣布他拿到金牌那一刻，原来还在厨房忙的人都停下来了，因为大家都知道，这个结果不是一两天突然得来的。

example_translations.translation: After she put that gold medal down properly, the family did not rush to speak first. What everyone wanted more was to know how she had managed to hold on through those final few minutes.

When the school invited her back to speak, she did not keep talking about how important the gold medal was. Instead, she first talked about those days when she most wanted to give up, yet still had to stand back up by herself.

At the moment television announced that he had won a gold medal, even the people who had still been busy in the kitchen stopped, because everyone knew that this result had not suddenly appeared in just a day or two.

glosses.notes: Refers to money in a broad, often more abstract way, especially when talking about value, pressure, temptation, or choices in life.

examples.sentence: 父亲常说，金钱当然重要，但是一个人如果为了多赚一点就把身体和家里的人全放在后面，最后多半还是不值。
那位老人年轻时吃过不少苦，所以现在看孩子花金钱的时候，总会先提醒一句，买东西以前最好先想想是不是真的用得上。
这件事让大家争了很久，表面上看像是在谈金钱，后来才有人指出，真正让人过不去的其实是心里那口气。

example_translations.translation: Father often says that money is important, of course, but if someone sacrifices their health and family just to earn a little more, it usually is not worth it in the end.

That old man suffered a lot when he was young, so now whenever he sees children spending money, he always reminds them first that before buying something, it is best to think about whether it will truly be useful.
This matter kept everyone arguing for a long time. On the surface it seemed to be about money, but later someone pointed out that what people really could not get past was their pride.

glosses.notes: Refers to finance as a field involving banks, investment, markets, and the movement or management of money in larger systems.

examples.sentence: 这座城近几年发展得很快，不只是因为路修得多，也是因为这里做金融的人越来越多，很多新公司也跟着进来了。
她原来学的不是金融，但是工作几年以后才发现，很多离自己很远的变化，最后都会一点一点影响到普通人的生活。
老师上课讲金融的时候，没有先把最难的词都写满黑板，而是先让大家看一个小城市的钱是怎么慢慢流动起来的。

example_translations.translation: This city has developed quickly in recent years not only because many roads have been built, but also because more and more people here work in finance, and many new companies have moved in along with them.
Finance was not what she originally studied, but after working for several years she realized that many changes that seem far removed from oneself eventually affect ordinary people little by little.
When the teacher taught finance in class, he did not first fill the blackboard with the hardest terms. Instead, he first let everyone look at how money in a small city slowly begins to circulate.

glosses.notes: Refers to metal as a material, whether in daily objects, buildings, machines, sound, or industrial settings.

examples.sentence: 老师把木头、玻璃和金属都拿出来，让学生一个一个去摸，因为只听名字的时候，很多人其实根本分不清差别。
门口那块旧金属牌子被风和雨打了很多年，字已经不算很清楚了，但是大家一看见它，还是会想起从前那家老店。
工人敲那块金属的时候，站在后面的人都能听出声音不太一样，所以负责人马上让大家停下来再看一遍里面是不是空了。

example_translations.translation: The teacher took out wood, glass, and metal and let the students touch them one by one, because when people hear only the names, many in fact cannot tell the differences at all.

That old metal sign by the doorway had been battered by wind and rain for many years, and the writing was no longer especially clear, but as soon as people saw it they still thought of the old shop from before.

When the worker knocked on that piece of metal, even the people standing behind could hear that the sound was a little different, so the person in charge immediately had everyone stop and check once more whether the inside had become hollow.

glosses.notes: Refers to gold as a precious material, and it also appears in comparisons about value, shine, or something truly worth keeping.

examples.sentence: 老人把那只小盒子拿出来的时候，孩子们原来都以为里面会有很多金子，打开以后才发现，他最想留下来的其实是一张旧照片。
她常说，一个人是不是真像金子一样，不是看顺的时候说得多好，重点是难的时候会不会乱。
店里那条旧项链看上去并不特别亮，但是老板一说里面真有金子，旁边原来只是看看的几个人一下子都认真起来了。

example_translations.translation: When the old man took out that small box, the children had all assumed there would be a lot of gold inside, but only after opening it did they discover that what he most wanted to keep was actually an old photograph.
She often says that whether a person is truly like gold is not judged by how well that person speaks when things are going smoothly, but by whether they lose control when times are hard.

That old necklace in the shop did not look especially bright, but as soon as the owner said there was real gold in it, the few people nearby who had only been looking casually all suddenly became serious.

glosses.notes: This word often appears in forms like 用尽, 尽量, and 尽快, showing either exhausting something completely or doing something as fully or as quickly as possible.

examples.sentence: 为了把最后那点时间用尽，老师没有让大家提前收东西，而是一直讲到下课前一分钟，连后排的人都不敢走神。
医生看完以后说，现在最重要的不是乱想，大家尽量先把饭吃下去，先把身体养好，因为身体一乱，别的事也会跟着更难。
负责人知道消息一出来就会有人着急，所以他一进门就让大家先坐下，然后尽快把现在已经确定的部分一个一个讲清楚。

example_translations.translation: In order to use up the last bit of time, the teacher did not let everyone start putting things away early, but kept teaching until one minute before class ended, and even the people in the back did not dare lose focus.

After the examination, the doctor said that what mattered most now was not letting the mind run wild. Everyone should first try their utmost to eat properly and get the body back in shape, because once the body becomes unsettled, everything else also becomes harder.

The person in charge knew that people would grow anxious as soon as the news came out, so the moment he entered he had everyone sit down first and then explained one by one, as quickly as possible, the parts that had already been confirmed.

glosses.notes: Used to show that one thing leads on to a further step, result, or level, often in formal explanation or reasoning.

examples.sentence: 老师先让大家把最表面的意思听懂，进而再带着全班往深一点的地方想，这样原来最怕这页的人后来也敢开口了。
他们先把旧照片一张一张整理好，进而才开始讨论到底哪些东西值得留下，因为要是前后顺序一乱，后面就更难说清。
医生没有一上来就下结论，而是先看最近几天的变化，进而再提醒家里人，后面哪些地方需要继续特别注意。

example_translations.translation: The teacher first helped everyone understand the most basic meaning, and then led the whole class to think on a deeper level, so that later even the people who had feared this page most dared to speak.

They first sorted the old photos one by one, and only then began discussing which things were worth keeping, because once the order gets confused, everything afterward becomes harder to explain clearly.

The doctor did not jump to a conclusion right away. Instead, he first looked at the changes over the past few days and then reminded the family which things would need continued special attention afterward.

glosses.notes: Refers to the pace or stage of progress in work, study, construction, repair, or any longer process with steps to complete.

examples.sentence: 负责人下午又来看了一次进度，不是因为不相信大家，而是因为这几天雨太多，很多原来安排好的时间都得跟着重算。
老师知道这页很难，所以一直没有急着把进度往前赶，而是先停下来问后排的人是不是也已经跟上了。
工程前面看上去进度不快，但是后来大家才发现，很多时间都花在那些很容易被忽略的小问题上。

example_translations.translation: The person in charge came again in the afternoon to check the progress, not because he distrusted everyone, but because there had been too much rain over the past few days and many originally planned times now had to be recalculated.
The teacher knew this page was difficult, so she did not rush to push the progress forward, but instead stopped first to ask whether the people in the back had also caught up.
The project did not seem to be making fast progress at first, but later everyone discovered that a great deal of time had been spent on those small problems that are very easily overlooked.

glosses.notes: Can refer to biological evolution over a very long time, and it can also be used more broadly for gradual development into a more complex form.

examples.sentence: 老师讲到动物怎么一步一步进化的时候，没有先让学生背最难的名字，而是先让大家看最简单的变化是从哪里开始的。
这座城最近几年变化很快，不过老人常说，它不是一天突然变成现在这样，而是很多小地方一点一点进化过来的。
孩子问人为什么会和从前不一样，父亲没有马上给标准答案，只是先讲进化这个过程本来就慢，很多变化要很久以后才看得出来。

example_translations.translation: When the teacher talked about how animals evolved step by step, she did not first make the students memorize the hardest names, but instead showed everyone where the simplest changes had begun.

This city has changed quickly in recent years, but the older people often say it did not suddenly become what it is today in a single day; rather, many small parts gradually evolved into it little by little.

When the child asked why people are different from the past, the father did not immediately give a standard answer. He first explained that the process of evolution is naturally slow and that many changes only become visible after a long time.

glosses.notes: Means recently or in the period close to now, often when describing noticeable changes in mood, health, work, or public life.

examples.sentence: 他近来总是睡得不太好，所以白天一坐下来就容易走神，连平时最简单的事也得别人再提醒一遍。
这家店近来看书的人越来越多，老板原来还怕店太小，后来却发现，真正让人留下来的还是这里很安静。
老师上课的时候提到，近来大家说话都比从前快了很多，所以越是重要的事，越得慢一点讲，不然很容易听错。

example_translations.translation: Recently he has not been sleeping very well, so during the day he gets distracted as soon as he sits down, and even the simplest things now have to be reminded to him one more time.

Recently more and more people have been coming to read at this shop. The owner had originally worried the shop was too small, but later discovered that what truly kept people there was how quiet it was.

The teacher mentioned in class that recently everyone has been speaking much faster than before, so the more important something is, the more slowly it needs to be said, otherwise it is easy to hear it wrongly.

glosses.notes: Describes being nearsighted, and it often comes up in discussions about eye health, screens, reading habits, or wearing glasses.

examples.sentence: 医生提醒家里的人，孩子如果已经有一点近视，就不能只怪书多或者灯不亮，还得看他平时坐得对不对、休息够不够。
她小时候一直不愿意戴眼镜，总觉得自己只是看远一点不清楚，后来老师把她调到前面，她才承认自己可能真的近视了。
学校最近做检查的时候，不少家长一听见近视这个词就先紧张了，其实医生后面说得更清楚，最要紧的是早点改习惯。

example_translations.translation: The doctor reminded the family that if the child was already a little nearsighted, they could not blame only too many books or dim light; they also had to look at whether he usually sat properly and rested enough.

When she was little, she never wanted to wear glasses and always felt that she simply could not see very far clearly. Only after the teacher moved her to the front did she admit that she might really be nearsighted.

When the school recently conducted examinations, many parents became nervous as soon as they heard the word nearsighted, though the doctor later explained more clearly that what mattered most was changing habits early.

glosses.notes: Refers to progress or development in a situation, plan, conversation, repair, or investigation, especially when something is gradually moving forward.

examples.sentence: 这件事原来卡了很久，不过今天终于有了一点进展，所以负责人一回来就把大家叫到一起，先讲最确定的那部分。
医生看完片子以后说，现在还不能把话说得太满，不过比起前几天，病情确实已经有了进展，后面可以慢慢往前走。
老师怕后排那几个学生听不懂，后来一看，他们也开始说话了，才觉得已经有了一点进展。

example_translations.translation: This matter had been stuck for a long time, but today there was finally some progress, so as soon as the person in charge came back, everyone was called together and the most certain part was explained first.

After looking at the scan, the doctor said that it was still too early to speak too confidently, but compared with a few days ago, the condition had indeed made progress and things could move forward slowly afterward.

The teacher was afraid that the few students in the back would not understand, but later, when she took another look and saw they had also begun to speak, she felt that things had finally made a little progress.

glosses.notes: Describes something beautifully made with fine detail, such as objects, food, decoration, design, or printed materials.

examples.sentence: 这家小店地方不大，但是柜子里那些做得很精美的小东西总会让路过的人停下来，因为一看就知道花了很多时间。
老师把那本画册慢慢翻开的时候，学生们先注意到的不是纸有多厚，而是里面每一页都画得特别精美。
那几个很普通的小点心一切开，大家才发现里面做得非常精美，所以连原来不饿的人也忍不住先吃了一口。

example_translations.translation: This little shop is not large, but those exquisitely made small objects in the cabinet always make passersby stop, because one glance shows that a great deal of time went into them.
When the teacher slowly opened that art album, what the students noticed first was not how thick the paper was, but how exquisitely every page inside had been drawn.

Only after those quite ordinary-looking pastries were cut open did everyone discover how exquisitely they had been made, so that even the people who had not been hungry could not resist taking a bite first.

glosses.notes: Describes something as accurate and exact, whether it is a number, time, measurement, explanation, or judgment.

examples.sentence: 医生说现在最难的不是没有答案，大家只是太着急想要一个精确时间，但是很多变化本来就得慢慢看。
老师提醒学生，写报告的时候不能只觉得差不多就行，越是重要的数字，越要尽量精确，不然前面做的事都会白费。
那位老人讲起从前的路时，方向和距离都说得非常精确，所以年轻人一边听一边看图，后来真的一点没走错。

example_translations.translation: The doctor said that the hardest thing right now was not the lack of an answer. People were simply too eager to have an exact time, even though many changes naturally have to be observed slowly.

The teacher reminded the students that when writing a report, they cannot feel that “close enough” is fine. The more important a number is, the more precise they should try to be, otherwise all the work done earlier may be wasted.

When that old man talked about the roads from the past, he described both the direction and the distance very accurately, so the young people listened while looking at the map and later truly did not go wrong at all.

glosses.notes: Describes something as astonishing in size, speed, ability, change, or effect, often beyond what people originally expected.

examples.sentence: 这孩子平时话不算多，但是一到台上就把整段都背出来了，老师站在旁边听完以后，也觉得记忆力真是惊人。
河水退下去以后，大家看见桥居然还站得住，都觉得这座老桥的力量实在惊人，因为前一天谁也不敢这样想。
医生后来解释说，身体恢复的速度之所以这么惊人，不是因为运气突然变好，而是前面每一天都真的按要求做了。

example_translations.translation: This child is not especially talkative in daily life, but once on stage he recited the whole passage, and after listening from the side, even the teacher felt that his memory was truly astonishing.

After the river water went down, everyone saw that the bridge was somehow still standing and felt that the strength of that old bridge was astonishing, because the day before no one had dared imagine that.
The doctor later explained that the reason the speed of recovery was so astonishing was not that luck had suddenly improved, but that every day beforehand the instructions had truly been followed.

glosses.notes: Means to engage in business or trade, often with attention to experience, risk, judgment, and how one deals with people over time.

examples.sentence: 他年轻时就跟着家里人到外地经商，所以看人说话的时候总比别人慢一点，因为他知道很多事不能只听表面。
老人常说，经商最难的不是一开始把东西卖出去，而是后面出了小问题以后，人家还愿不愿意再相信你一次。
她原来只想安安静静做老师，后来因为家里有事，不得不回去帮忙经商，这才发现自己原来最不擅长的是天天和人谈钱。

example_translations.translation: When he was young he followed his family to other places to do business, so when listening to people speak he is still slower to judge than others, because he knows many things cannot be understood from the surface alone.

The old man often says that the hardest part of doing business is not selling the goods at the beginning, but whether after a small problem arises later, people are still willing to trust you one more time.

She had originally only wanted to be a quiet teacher, but later, because something happened in the family, she had no choice but to go back and help with business. Only then did she discover that what she was worst at was talking about money with people every day.

glosses.notes: Means to know a subject, skill, language, or technique very well through long study and practice, not just basic familiarity.

examples.sentence: 老师说，真正精通一门外语的人，不是只会把书上的句子背下来，而是换个地方、换个人以后，也能自然地说清。
他平时不太爱说话，但是一讲到机器怎么修，大家就知道他是真的精通，因为很多地方别人根本想不到。
这位老人并没有正式上过很多学，但是他对这条老街以前的事非常精通，连年轻的导游都愿意先站在旁边听他讲。

example_translations.translation: The teacher said that someone who truly masters a foreign language is not a person who can only recite sentences from a book, but someone who can still speak clearly and naturally when the place and the listener both change.

He does not usually like talking very much, but once he starts talking about how to repair machines, everyone knows he truly has mastery, because there are many points that other people would never think of at all.

This old man never formally studied very much, but he is extremely proficient in the earlier history of this old street, and even the younger guides are willing to stand nearby and listen to him first.

glosses.notes: Usually works like an adverb meaning carefully and with great attention, especially when planning, preparing, arranging, or making something by hand.

examples.sentence: 母亲精心准备了一下午，本来只想让家里的人安安静静吃饭，没想到大家一坐下来，就先注意到她做的那些菜。
老师为了这次活动精心排了很久，不是想让场面看上去多热闹，而是怕真正轮到孩子上台时，前后会一下子乱掉。
这本书能让那么多人记住，不只是因为写得好，也是因为后面每一张图、每一行字都像是精心放在该在的位置上。

example_translations.translation: Mother prepared everything with great care all afternoon, originally only hoping the family could sit down and eat quietly together. Unexpectedly, once everyone sat down, the first thing they noticed was the dishes she had made.

The teacher spent a long time arranging this event meticulously, not to make the scene look especially lively, but because she was afraid that when it truly became the children’s turn to go on stage, everything before and after would suddenly fall into disorder.

What has made so many people remember this book is not only that it is well written, but also that every picture and every line afterward seems to have been carefully placed exactly where it should be.

glosses.notes: Describes feeling surprised or amazed by something unexpected, often because it is very different from what one had assumed before.

examples.sentence: 她原来以为老师早把那封信忘了，后来看到它还好好地放在盒子里时，惊讶得半天都不知道先说什么。
大家听见那个最安静的学生忽然站起来把整段都讲清楚时，都很惊讶，因为前一天他还说自己根本不敢开口。
父亲打开门看见多年没见的朋友居然站在外面，脸上的惊讶一下子就藏不住了，连手里拿着的东西都差点掉下来。

example_translations.translation: She had assumed the teacher had long forgotten that letter, and when she later saw it still carefully kept in the box, she was so surprised that for a long time she did not know what to say first.
Everyone was amazed when the quietest student suddenly stood up and explained the whole passage clearly, because only the day before he had said that he did not dare speak at all.
When Father opened the door and saw a friend he had not seen for many years standing outside, the surprise on his face instantly could not be hidden, and he almost dropped what he was holding.

glosses.notes: Describes something as finely made, well designed, and refined in appearance, detail, or craftsmanship.

examples.sentence: 那个小盒子看上去不大，但是做得十分精致，所以大家一拿起来，就忍不住先慢慢看一看再打开。
这家店的东西不一定都很贵，但是一看就让人舒服，所以人一坐下来，就会觉得整个地方特别精致。
老师把那件旧衣服拿出来给大家看时，学生们先注意到的不是颜色，而是上面那些做得很精致的小地方。

example_translations.translation: That small box did not look big, but it was made very delicately, so as soon as people picked it up, they could not resist slowly looking it over before opening it.
The things in this shop are not all necessarily expensive, but one look already makes people feel comfortable, so once they sit down, the whole place feels especially refined.
When the teacher took out that old piece of clothing for everyone to see, what the students noticed first was not the color, but those small parts on it that had been made so delicately.

glosses.notes: Describes something as very precise and sharply aimed, whether it is data, language, judgment, timing, or movement.

examples.sentence: 医生后来提醒家里的人，想帮病人并不是把话说得越多越好，很多时候真正有用的反而是那几句最精准的提醒。
老师改这篇报告的时候，一直强调最重要的不是句子有多长，而是每一个数字和判断是不是都足够精准。
那位老人指路时不太看地图，但是方向和时间都说得非常精准，所以第一次来的人后来也一点没有走错。

example_translations.translation: The doctor later reminded the family that helping a patient does not mean saying more and more words. Many times what is truly useful are instead those few reminders that are the most precise.
While revising this report, the teacher kept emphasizing that what mattered most was not how long the sentences were, but whether every figure and judgment was accurate enough.

When that old man gave directions, he did not look at the map very much, yet he described both the direction and the timing with great precision, so even the people visiting for the first time did not go wrong afterward at all.

glosses.notes: Refers to a water well, especially in villages, older neighborhoods, or scenes where daily life still depends on drawing water from the ground.

examples.sentence: 雨停了以后，村里的人先去看井里的水还能不能用，因为院子里那些东西就算全洗一遍，也没有这件事更要紧。
老人常说，他小时候每天最早听见的声音不是闹钟，而是有人站在井边慢慢打水，所以一到夏天就会特别想起从前。
导游带大家走到那口老井前面时，没有先讲名字，而是先让大家低头看看井有多深，再想想过去的人每天怎么过日子。

example_translations.translation: After the rain stopped, the people in the village first went to see whether the water in the well could still be used, because even if everything in the yard had to be washed again, nothing was more urgent than that.

The old man often says that when he was little, the first sound he heard each day was not an alarm clock, but someone slowly drawing water by the well, so every time summer comes he thinks especially of the past.

When the guide led everyone to that old well, he did not start by giving its name. Instead, he first had everyone lower their heads and see how deep it was, and then imagine how people in the past lived every day.

glosses.notes: Means to warn someone about danger, risk, or bad consequences so they will pay attention and change what they are doing.

examples.sentence: 医生已经警告过他很多次，说如果还是一直熬夜，后面就不只是白天没精神这么简单，身体迟早会真的受不了。
路边那块牌子虽然字不大，但是已经把最危险的地方警告得很清楚了，所以再往前走的人也不能说自己完全不知道。
老师先没有生气，而是把那件事后面可能带来的问题一个一个说出来，想用最明白的方式警告大家别再犯同样的错。

example_translations.translation: The doctor had already warned him many times, saying that if he kept staying up late, later it would not be only a matter of having no energy in the daytime, and sooner or later his body would truly be unable to take it.

Although the writing on that sign by the roadside was not large, it had already warned very clearly about the most dangerous area, so people who walked farther ahead could not say they had been completely unaware.

The teacher did not get angry at first, but instead explained one by one the problems that the matter could bring later, wanting to warn everyone in the clearest possible way not to make the same mistake again.

glosses.notes: Refers to a landscape or visual scene shaped by nature, design, or a city plan, often when discussing what people see in a place.

examples.sentence: 这条河原来只是安安静静地从城边过去，后来因为两边慢慢修起来，整个景观一下子就和从前很不一样了。
设计这块地方的人说，最难的不是多放几棵树，而是怎么让景观和大家平时真正会走的路自然连在一起。
站在桥上往下看时，孩子先注意到的不是高楼，而是水边那些颜色很慢才看出来的景观变化，所以一直不肯马上走。

example_translations.translation: This river originally just passed quietly by the edge of the city, but later, as both sides were gradually developed, the whole landscape suddenly became very different from before.

The person who designed this area said that the hardest part was not simply adding a few more trees, but figuring out how to connect the landscape naturally with the routes people actually use every day.

When standing on the bridge and looking down, what the child noticed first was not the tall buildings, but the changes in the landscape by the water whose colors only slowly came into view, and so he refused to leave right away.

glosses.notes: Refers to the scene or sight in front of the eyes, especially when many details together create a striking overall impression.

examples.sentence: 雨停以后大家一起走到外面，看见路上那种从安静一下变成热闹的景象时，谁都没有马上说话，只是先站着看。
老人说，他很多年以后还记得那天早上的景象，因为太阳刚出来、门刚打开、街上所有声音都像一下子醒过来了。
医生进门以后先没有急着开口，因为他一看见那个景象，就知道这时候最需要的是让人先坐下。

example_translations.translation: After the rain stopped, everyone walked outside together, and when they saw the scene of the road changing from quiet to lively all at once, no one spoke right away and simply stood there looking first.

The old man said that even many years later he still remembers the sight of that morning, because the sun had just risen, the doors had just opened, and every sound on the street seemed to wake up all at once.
After the doctor came in, he did not hurry to speak, because the moment he saw that scene, he knew that what was most needed at that moment was to let people sit down first.
